topic: What if you could catch a shooting star?
timely_hook: The Southern Taurid meteor shower peaks around 5 Nov 2026 and is known for bright fireballs; the Northern Taurids peak around 12 Nov 2026 (NASA "What's Up: November 2026").
title: WHAT IF YOU
COULD CATCH A STAR?

power.rule: you can pluck a shooting star straight out of the night sky into your bare hand
power.look: catch: a slow-motion streak freezing in your palm with a warm golden-cyan starlight halo, a CATCH HUD chip, and a soft chime

script.text: A streak of light over the park. You reach up. Catch. It's warm.
Your mate makes a wish. You hand it to him.
By midnight, your jar is glowing.
What if you could catch shooting stars?

script.beat: 4 the turn: the cost, one real fact
script.text: One catch. Taurid meteors hit the air at about 27 kilometres per second. That's over 25 times faster than a rifle bullet. That's real.
And tonight, something much bigger is heading your way.

science.claim: Taurid meteors hit the air at about 27 kilometres per second.
science.working: Southern Taurid (STA) meteoroids enter Earth's atmosphere at an average geocentric/entry velocity of about 27 km/s (Northern Taurids, NTA, are about 29 km/s).
science.source: International Meteor Organization (IMO) Meteor Shower Calendar / October–November 2026 outlook (STA: 27 km/s, NTA: 29 km/s)

science.claim: 27 km/s is over 25 times faster than a rifle bullet.
science.working: A typical rifle bullet muzzle speed is roughly 0.8 to 1.0 km/s (800–1,000 m/s) or less. 27 km/s ÷ 1.0 km/s = 27x (> 25x faster).
science.source: Standard rifle muzzle velocity (~0.8–1.0 km/s); arithmetic (27 / 1.0 = 27 > 25)

science.claim: The Southern Taurids peak around 5 November 2026 and the Northern Taurids peak around 12 November 2026, and the Taurids are known for bright fireballs.
science.working: Early November 2026 features the dual peaks of the Taurid meteor shower: Southern Taurids around Nov 5, 2026 and Northern Taurids around Nov 12, 2026, noted for bright fireball activity.
science.source: NASA "What's Up: November 2026" skywatching guide & IMO 2026 Meteor Shower Calendar
